1.title: Observability and Cost
1.text: Welcome to Module 13: Observability and Cost. This module is in the Cloud Native Architecture domain, and it covers the topic called Observability and Cost. By the end you will be able to do four things. Explain observability and the three signals: metrics, logs and traces. Describe Open Telemetry, Prometheus and Alertmanager. Define S L I, S L O, S L A and error budget. And name the Kubernetes signals, and the basics of Fin Ops and Open Cost.

1.title: Case Check-In: Harbor Books Wants to See Checkout
1.text: At Harbor Books, checkout feels slow for some customers. The team needs metrics, logs and traces for the orders service. Management wants a latency target for checkout, and a clear view of how often it is missed. And finance wants to understand the monthly cloud bill for the shop. In this module you learn how to see the system, and what it costs.

1.title: Monitoring, Observability and the Three Signals
1.text: Observability means understanding a system's internal state from its outputs. It lets you ask new questions, even about unknown unknowns. Monitoring watches known signals, and alerts when they go wrong. Three signals feed both. Metrics are numbers aggregated over time, such as error rate, C P U use and request rate. Logs are timestamped messages. Traces follow one request through services, and are made of spans. The code must be instrumented to emit these signals. Exam tip: metrics tell you that, logs tell you what, and traces tell you where.

1.title: OpenTelemetry: API, SDK and Collector
1.text: Open Telemetry, or O Tel, is an open source, vendor-neutral framework to generate, export and collect traces, metrics and logs. It is not a backend. Storing and showing the data is left to tools such as Prometheus and Jaeger. The A P I and the S D K, the software development kit, instrument the code. O T L P is the standard protocol, and semantic conventions name common data. The Collector receives, processes and exports data, so a service can hand it off quickly. The project grew out of Open Tracing and Open Census. Exam tip: Open Telemetry produces telemetry, and it does not store it.

1.title: Prometheus: Pull, Exporters and PromQL
1.text: This slide is tagged archived topic. Prometheus is an open-source monitoring and alerting toolkit. It keeps metrics as time series, with labels. It pulls, or scrapes, metrics over H T T P from targets. A Pushgateway serves short-lived jobs. Exporters expose metrics for services that have none of their own, and targets come from service discovery. Prom Q L queries the time series. And there are four metric types. A counter only goes up. A gauge goes up and down. A histogram counts observations in buckets. And a summary calculates quantiles. Exam tip: Prometheus pulls, and a counter only goes up.

1.title: Alerting and the Tool Landscape
1.text: Five tools to recognize. Alertmanager takes alerts from Prometheus, then deduplicates, groups and routes them to receivers such as email or Pager Duty. Grafana draws dashboards, querying and visualizing metrics wherever they are stored. Fluent Bit is a lightweight agent that collects, processes and forwards logs, metrics and traces. Fluentd is an open-source log collector that unifies logging. And Jaeger is a distributed tracing platform. Prometheus decides that an alert fires, and Alertmanager decides who hears about it. Exam tip: Alertmanager routes alerts, and Grafana draws dashboards.

1.title: SLI, SLO, SLA and Error Budgets
1.text: Three terms, and one budget. An S L I is a service level indicator: a measurement of a service's behavior, ideally from the user's point of view. An S L O is a service level objective: the target for an S L I, and the way reliability is communicated. An S L A is a service level agreement: a contract with users, with consequences if the objectives are missed. The error budget is one hundred percent minus the S L O. It is the unreliability you may spend, and when it is used up, you put stability first. One hundred percent is the wrong target. Exam tip: S L I measures, S L O targets, S L A promises.

1.title: Kubernetes Signals
1.text: Kubernetes gives you five signals. Metrics Server provides resource metrics, the C P U and memory of Pods and nodes, for autoscaling and kube control top. It is not a monitoring system. Kube state metrics gives metrics about the state of objects, not the health of the components. Events, listed with kube control get events, tell you what happened to an object. The audit log tells you who did what through the A P I. And logs show what containers, the kube let and the control plane printed. Exam tip: Metrics Server for autoscaling, and kube state metrics for object state.

1.title: Cost Management and FinOps
1.text: This slide is tagged archived topic. Fin Ops is an operational framework and cultural practice. Engineering, finance and business share accountability for technology spend. Open Cost is an open source project that shows what Kubernetes and cloud resources cost, now and over time, and how the spend is allocated across applications and teams. Requests and limits, from Module 4, and autoscaling, from Module 5, shape what a workload reserves, and so what it costs. Cost needs the same visibility as reliability: measure first, then decide. Exam tip: Fin Ops is a practice, and Open Cost is a tool for seeing spend.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: To recap. Observability means understanding the inside from the outside, through metrics, logs and traces. Open Telemetry generates, exports and collects telemetry. The Collector is the hub, and it is not a backend. Prometheus pulls time series, uses Prom Q L, has four metric types, and Alertmanager routes alerts. Grafana, Fluent Bit, Fluentd and Jaeger are the other tools. S L I measures, S L O targets, S L A promises, and the error budget is one hundred percent minus the S L O. And Kubernetes signals are Metrics Server, kube state metrics, events and the audit log, with Fin Ops and Open Cost for cost. Now five practice questions.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which signal shows the path of a single request through several services? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. A distributed trace follows one request as it propagates through services, and is built from spans. Metrics aggregate numbers, logs are messages, and Kubernetes events describe changes to objects.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. What does Open Telemetry provide, and what does it leave to other tools? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Open Telemetry is a vendor-neutral framework for generating, exporting and collecting traces, metrics and logs. It is not a backend, so storage and visualization are left to tools such as Prometheus, Jaeger and Grafana.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. How does Prometheus normally collect metrics? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Prometheus uses a pull model. It scrapes metrics over H T T P from its targets. Pushing is supported only through an intermediary gateway for short-lived jobs, and the Alertmanager only handles alerts.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Harbor Books measures how long checkout takes, and then sets a target for that measurement. What are the two called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. An S L I is a measurement of a service's behavior, and an S L O is the target for it. An S L A is a contract with consequences if the objectives are missed, and the error budget is one hundred percent minus the S L O.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What does Open Cost provide? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Open Cost shows teams what Kubernetes and cloud resources cost, and how spend is allocated across applications and teams. It does not scale Pods, encrypt data or query metrics.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are the answers at a glance. Question one, B: traces follow a request through services. Question two, D: it generates, exports and collects, and it is not a backend. Question three, A: Prometheus pulls over H T T P. Question four, C: an S L I measures, and an S L O is the target. Question five, B: Open Cost shows Kubernetes and cloud spend.
